SIGNAL & RANKING controls · Facebook · trust & safety

I shipped a four-year-stalled redesign to 3 billion users in four months.

Facebook's 3-dot menu is how billions of users tell Feed what they do and don't want. 44% of user feedback called it confusing. I led a four-year-stalled redesign from 14+ fragmented actions to four core controls, while protecting the ranking and integrity signals the product depended on.

Simplified 14+ core controls down to 4 above the fold, shipped 1:1 as designed.
100% global rollout to 3B+ users.
+20% signal-quality improvement negative user feedback from the UI alone.
4 months from restart to global launch.

01 · Overview

I owned Facebook's most-used control surface, end to end.

Sole designer on the 3-dot menu, across every Facebook surface. I partnered with one eng lead, data scientists, and 10+ cross-functional teams: Feed, Reels, Groups, Marketplace, Privacy, Integrity, and Risk.

02 · The problem

The most-used menu was also the least trusted.

Years of additions had turned a high-frequency control surface into a scrolling inventory. Users found it overwhelming, while every team had metrics tied to keeping its action visible.

44%
of the words people used to describe the menu were negative: confusing, overwhelming, pushy.
03 · Context

Everyone had a stake. No one would give anything up.

10+ teams, all with something to lose, none willing to concede. It had been escalated and championed before, and still no one could get every team on the same page.

"Escalated, championed, and still stuck for four years. Until this."

With the eng lead, I built risk assessments and signal projections showing each team what the change meant for their numbers. No controls were deleted, only rehomed.

The north star

Every control mapped to a job, and a tier.

Each control mapped to a job and a tier, the structure that decides what belongs in the menu and what lives one layer down.
ALIGNMENT · STRUCTURE & ELEMENTS

Shipped globally, without compromising the simplification.
